Question Choices: Fill: Using Elimination, solve: $x + y = 14$ and $x - y = 4$. Find $x$.
Hints: Add equations when opposite coefficients cancel the requested variable.
Solution: System: x+y=14; x-y=4. Multiply equation 1 by 1 and equation 2 by 1, then add to cancel y: (2)x=18, so x=9. Substitute back to obtain y=5. Check both equations: 1(9)+1(5)=14; 1(9)+-1(5)=4. Requested answer: 9.

Question Choices: True or False: A system of parallel lines has exactly one solution. (True/False)
Hints: Use equivalent line equations: identical lines, distinct parallel lines, or one intersection.
Solution: Two distinct parallel lines never meet, so they have zero common points and no system solution. Crossing lines have one solution; coincident lines have infinitely many. Requested answer: False.

Hints: Set the equations equal since both equal $y$: $x - 2 = -3x + 10$
Solution: System: y=x-2; y=-3 × x+10. Isolate y: y=(1)x+(-2). Substitute into the other equation: (3)x+(1)[(1)x+(-2)]=10. Combine: (4)x=12, so x=3. Then y=(1)(3)+(-2)=1. Check both equations: -1(3)+1(1)=-2; 3(3)+1(1)=10. Requested answer: 3.
